title: Interactive project map
brief: A focused way to explore project dependencies and understand how the pieces fit together.
content:
## The approach

Build a lightweight graph of files and dependencies. Keep the first release small and make the relationships easy to follow.

> Make the relationships clear before adding ways to edit them.

## Exploring the graph

Use [React Flow](input:library) to render the graph. Start with [pan, zoom, and drag](input:interaction) so people can arrange the map as they explore.

1. **Render the project.** Show files and dependencies as a readable network of nodes and edges.
2. **Make it explorable.** Follow connections without losing your place in the project.
3. **Keep the context.** Show a file’s path and its immediate dependencies when selected.

## Validation

Before shipping, run [essential checks](input:testing) on the core workflow. Verify that the graph loads, nodes move correctly, and the layout survives a refresh.

## Remembering the layout

Keep layout persistence [enabled](input:persistence). Save node positions after each drag and restore them when the project is reopened.

### A small, durable model

Store positions by project ID, separate from the graph data. If a file disappears, discard its saved position; leave the rest of the layout intact.

## Boundaries

[Use an existing library for layout.](input:constraints) Defer collaborative editing and custom layout algorithms until the core experience proves useful.

previews.React Flow: Nodes, edges, and familiar interactions out of the box.
previews.Cytoscape.js: Graph analysis with a broad choice of layouts.

previews.0: A read-only picture of the project.
previews.1: Explore the graph without rearranging it.
previews.2: Pan, zoom, and move nodes into a useful arrangement.
previews.3: Focus the map on selected files and relationships.
previews.4: Find files and arrange the graph automatically.
previews.5: Organize related files and work on the map together.

previews.0: Verify the main workflow by hand.
previews.4: Cover edge cases and browser regressions.
previews.5: Include integration, accessibility, and performance coverage.
